name: Rovo Dev CLI

surfaces.label: Atlassian for VS Code extension (atlassian.atlascode) Rovo Dev panel. The extension downloads a standalone binary and runs it as a local HTTP server, one per workspace: <workspaceStorage>/atlassian.atlascode/atlascode-rovodev-bin/<version>/atlassian_cli_rovodev serve <port 40000-41000> --xid rovodev-ide-vscode --site-url https://<site> [--respect-configured-permissions]. On macOS <workspaceStorage> is under ~/Library/Application Support/<host>/User/workspaceStorage/, a path with a space, so a ps-based reader that splits args on spaces sees the executable as .../Library/Application; the pattern below therefore also matches that fragment and relies on args_contain to stay specific. Also runs in VS Code forks that load the extension (Cursor has it installed on this Mac); the fork's bundle id is the host, not the agent.

acli rovodev run (interactive terminal UI; `acli rovodev run <instruction>` is the one-shot non-interactive form, `--web` swaps the TUI for a web UI). Executable is the Go binary `acli`; an `atlassian_cli_rovodev` process (embedded or downloaded plugin) may appear as its child or in its place, so both names are listed. Short-lived `acli rovodev auth|config|mcp` also match while they run.

acli rovodev serve <port> (server mode, docs use the bare form `rovodev serve 8123`): local HTTP API, used by third-party wrappers such as gnhf and opencode-rovodev-auth, usually with --disable-session-token. Turn state is only visible over HTTP, not in the process table. Keep this surface after the tui surface: args_contain is a substring test, so `acli rovodev run fix the server config` also satisfies it, and the tui surface (which excludes only an exact `serve` argument) must claim it first.
Rovo Dev in Jira, Bitbucket, GitHub (rovo-dev-action) and the Rovo Dev web experience: nothing runs on this Mac

working_signals.meaning: Inferred, not observed: a bash tool call should run as a child of the agent process while a turn is executing a command. Blind while the model streams or thinks. Rovo Dev spawns long-lived MCP server children (the healthcheck lists filesystem-tools, atlassian and bitbucket servers), so this may fire on an idle process; treat as weak until seen on a live instance.
Inferred: session_context.json holds the full conversation, so it should be rewritten as a turn progresses. Write cadence (per step or per turn end) is not documented.
Fallback. Guess: the docs' config example shows console theme `textual-dark`, which suggests a Textual-based TUI that may redraw while idle; no doc or source says so, so the floor is a guess.

waiting_signals.meaning: Fires when the agent needs the user to approve a tool call (documented by Atlassian: 'blocked while waiting for user permission'). Default toolPermissions is ask, so this is the common stall.
Server mode only: GET /v3/stream_chat?pause_on_call_tools_start=true pauses until POST /v3/resume_tool_calls allows or denies. Seen in the Atlassian VS Code extension source (responseParser.ts).
NOT a turn-level permission wait: the extension uses it for MCP server terms that need accepting (POST /accept-mcp-terms). Do not treat as waiting-on-human for a running turn.

hooks.config: ~/.rovodev/config.yml, key eventHooks.events[] with name and commands[].command; edit interactively with /hooks. The event hooks log path is listed under eventHooks in /config. Payload is JSON on stdin (attributes.transcript_path, attributes.tool_input); the transcript file is deleted once the hook command exits.

telemetry.how: Unknown. No OpenTelemetry export is documented or exposed as a user setting (absence of evidence). A third-party reverse-engineering README lists LogFire (OpenTelemetry-based) among the embedded agent's dependencies, unverified. For local signals use eventHooks or the serve-mode HTTP stream.

sources.claim: Rovo Dev CLI is an extension of ACLI; run with `acli rovodev run`; auth with `acli rovodev auth login`
ACLI on macOS is a single binary named acli (Homebrew tap atlassian/homebrew-acli, or curl to /usr/local/bin/acli)
Command surface: run, run <instruction>, run --web, run --restore [id], run --yolo, run --worktree, run --config-file, serve [port], config, mcp; /hooks, /status, /sessions

Sessions stored under ~/.rovodev/sessions/ (configurable via sessions.persistenceDir) as session_context.json (full conversation) and metadata.json (title, workspace, fork info); sessions are per workspace; restore by UUID with `acli rovodev run --restore <UUID>`; UUID shown by /status as Session ID

The per-session subdirectory (~/.rovodev/sessions/<uuid>/) is inferred: the docs name the directory and the two file names but not the nesting. The session_context.json content shape (message_history[].kind, parts[].part_kind) is inferred from a third-party adapter reading the hook transcript, and the JSON vs JSONL distinction rests on the .json file name
sources.evidence: inferred; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PeonPing/peon-ping/main/adapters/rovodev.sh (jq over .message_history / .parts / .part_kind). Not verified: no Rovo Dev install or session store exists on this Mac (ls ~/.rovodev printed 'No such file or directory')

sources.claim: Config at ~/.rovodev/config.yml, MCP config at ~/.rovodev/mcp_config.json (docs) or mcp.json (extension), log at ~/.rovodev/logs/rovodev.log; toolPermissions default is ask

Standalone binary is named atlassian_cli_rovodev, downloaded from https://acli.atlassian.com/plugins/rovodev/<platform>/<arch>/<version>/rovodev.zip into <extension storage>/atlascode-rovodev-bin/<version>/, and spawned as `atlassian_cli_rovodev serve <port> --xid rovodev-ide-vscode --site-url https://<host> --respect-configured-permissions` with cwd = workspace and env ROVODEV_SERVE_SESSION_TOKEN; ports 40000-41000

Two installed extension builds exist. atlascode 4.0.32 (in ~/.cursor/extensions, the current one) pins Rovo Dev 202607.24.1 and matches the public source: child_process spawn of atlassian_cli_rovodev with `serve <port> --xid rovodev-ide-vscode --site-url https://<host> --respect-configured-permissions`, env ROVODEV_SERVE_SESSION_TOKEN. atlascode 3.8.18 (in ~/.vscode/extensions, stale) pins 0.11.24 and instead opens a hidden VS Code terminal with shellPath = the binary, no --respect-configured-permissions and no session token; the site-url argument is wrapped in literal double quotes there

Search of build/extension/extension.js in 4.0.32 found `"--xid"`, `--respect-configured-permissions`, `ROVODEV_SERVE_SESSION_TOKEN` and a spawn(...) call, and no createTerminal({name:"Rovo Dev"; in 3.8.18 it found createTerminal({name:"Rovo Dev",shellPath:this.rovoDevBinPath,shellArgs:["serve",...,"--xid","rovodev-ide-vscode","--site-url",g]}) and no ROVODEV_SERVE_SESSION_TOKEN. Neither binary is downloaded (no atlassian.atlascode dir under ~/Library/Application Support/{Code,Cursor}/User/workspaceStorage)

notes: Nothing here was seen on a running instance: Rovo Dev is not installed on this Mac and the CLI is closed source, so the working signals are inferred and the process names rest on docs, the VS Code extension source and one third-party report. Verify on a live install before trusting any detector built from this row: run `ps -axo pid=,ppid=,args=` during a turn, and `lsof -p <pid> -a -d cwd`. session_store.documented is false: the docs name ~/.rovodev/sessions/ and the file names session_context.json and metadata.json but not the per-session subdirectory, so the glob is inferred (two fixed file names per session make one directory per session likely). Process matching caveats: (1) surface order matters, keep tui before daemon, because args_contain is a substring test; a one-shot instruction that contains the exact word `serve` is still read as a server. (2) The IDE surface matches the fragment '/Library/Application' only in combination with args_contain atlascode-rovodev-bin and serve; that fragment exists only because the probe cuts argv[0] at the first space, and a reader using the full executable path matches '/atlascode-rovodev-bin/' directly. (3) The name `acli` is shared with Acquia CLI (docs.acquia.com, `acli auth:login`); args_contain rovodev keeps it out, but any acli command whose arguments mention rovodev would match. (4) Helper processes started by the agent (MCP servers) are ignored only while their parent still matches; reparented orphans could show as extra sessions. Unverified. Hook payload facts (stdin JSON, attributes.transcript_path, transcript deleted after the hook exits, ROVODEV_SESSION_ID) and all event names except on_tool_permission come from the peon-ping adapter, not from Atlassian. In server mode the exact answer for 'is a turn in progress' is over HTTP: hold GET /v3/stream_chat open or watch for tool-call events; the extension sets ROVODEV_SERVE_SESSION_TOKEN (current build) so requests need that token unless started with --disable-session-token. Map a process to its session by the --restore value when present (the flag's value is optional and a fresh session has no id in argv), by the port in `serve <port>` plus GET /healthcheck x-session-id, or by matching the process cwd against the workspace recorded in each session's metadata.json. The session directory can be moved with sessions.persistenceDir and the config file with --config-file. Version drift: the server-mode doc example shows 0.11.26, the stale extension pins 0.11.24 and the current one pins 202607.24.1, so the Rovo Dev version scheme has changed.
